text: The app is big. I started downloading it at home and it finished almost my whole {data_amount} bundle before it even opened. Then it wanted an update straight away. I didn't even get to see what it does yet.
My phone can't take apps. The lady at the branch said I must just download it. I told her, with what?
It asked me to make a username, then a password, then a PIN, then another PIN for the app. Why four things? I'm going to forget at least two of them.
The password rules only came up after I got it wrong. Eight letters, a capital, a sign... why not tell me before I start typing? I tried three times and then it said I must wait.
Downloading was fine. Signing up took me long, maybe {minutes}, because I had to go find my ID in the drawer. Not really the app's fault.
It was quicker than I thought. I put my number, got the SMS, and I was in. I was expecting a whole long story.
My granddaughter helped me with the first part but after that I did it myself. The writing is big enough and it tells you one thing at a time. It didn't rush me, that I liked.
The letters are too small for me. I had to take off my glasses, put them back. Some of the buttons I didn't even see they were buttons.
It's okay. Normal app stuff.
It closed by itself twice when I went out to check my SMS. Each time, back to the beginning.
Smooth, honestly. Fingerprint setup was one tap. I've seen worse from banks.
For a bank app now it feels slow. Every screen loads like it's thinking about it. Same phone, {other_bank} opens faster.

I wasn't sure if it's the real app because there were two that looked the same in the store. I checked the reviews first. Maybe put something that shows this is the real one, because people get scammed like that.
It said "create your profile". I didn't know if that's the same as opening an account or something else. I just pressed next.
Easy. Didn't need help.
After I registered it took me to a screen with lots of things and I didn't know what to press to actually open the account.
It works. Nothing special, nothing bad. I just wanted it done so I could get my money in.
I'm not good with phones but this one I managed. Every page had one question only. When I made a mistake it showed me where, in red. I didn't have to call {family}.

Where I stay the network comes and goes. Every time it dropped, the app said "something went wrong" and I had to start again. I tried in the morning, I tried at night. In the end I went to town to use the wifi at the mall.
Registering was easy until it asked for my ID number. I don't have a South African ID. There was no place for a passport, so I stopped there.
Too many screens just to say hello.
I liked that it sent an SMS to check it's me. It makes me feel it's not just anybody who can open in my name.
I typed my name, surname and ID number, and then two screens later it asked for my surname again. Then my date of birth, which is already in the ID number. Don't you have it already?
There was a question "marital regime" or something like that. I didn't understand it. I chose the first one.
Normal questions. Name, address, email. It's long but I understand why the bank wants it.
It wanted an email address and I don't have one. I made one quickly on Gmail but now I don't remember the password for that either.
It already filled my name and birthday from the ID. I just checked and pressed next. That was nice.
My address doesn't fit the boxes. We don't have a street number at home, it's a stand number and the village name. It kept saying invalid address. I ended up putting my aunt's address in town.
One page had like ten boxes. On a small phone that's a lot of scrolling and I missed one, so it shouted at me in red at the bottom.
Fast. Just the basics.
Why does it need to know my race and my marital status just to open an account? I answered, but I don't like it. Maybe say why you need it.
The keyboard covered the box I was typing in, so I couldn't see what I was writing. I just hoped it was right.
I liked that it showed an example under each box, like "e.g. 0821234567". I always get confused about putting the 0 or the 27. This time I knew.
It said "invalid" but not what's wrong.
It asked for my employer's name. I don't have an employer, I sell. I wrote "self" and it went through, so I guess it's fine.
I was halfway when a call came in. When I came back everything I typed was gone. I swear I nearly threw the phone. I did it again but only because I really need the account.
I left it in the middle to cook and when I came back it was still there where I left. That I didn't expect.
Just forms. Fine.
It only accepts a 13-digit ID. My permit number has letters, so it won't take it. There's no other option.
I did it while the kids were busy. It's long but at least I could stop and start.

It kept saying "image unclear, try again". I tried by the window, I tried with the light on, I put the ID on a white page. Like eight times. At the end I gave up and tried again the next day and it worked first time. I don't know what changed.
My ID is the green book. It's old and the photo page is a bit faded. The app couldn't read it. Must I go to Home Affairs just to open a bank account?
The frame on the screen showed me exactly where to put the card. It took the picture by itself. Easy.
It took three tries but it worked. The first ones my hand was shaking.
My phone camera is not good. Everything comes out blurry. I had to use {family}'s phone for the picture.
I liked that it scanned the Smart ID front and back and then checked it with Home Affairs straight away. I got a tick within seconds. That's how it should work.
The camera part took forever.
Each time it uploaded the photo it took long and I could see my data going down. Then it failed and I had to take it again and upload again. I felt like I was paying the bank to open the account.
I wasn't sure if it wanted the front only or the back as well, so I took both. Then it asked again for the back. Maybe tell me upfront: front, then back.
There's no option for a passport. Only SA ID, green ID or Smart ID. So what do people like me do?
Took a picture, done.
It said "document not supported". My Smart ID is new. Not supported how?
I was scared for this part but it told me "hold still" and it just took it. I didn't even have to press.
I don't like taking photos of my ID on an app. You hear about people's IDs being used for loans. But it's a bank, so okay.
At night in my room there's only one globe, so the picture had a shine on the card and it kept rejecting. It never said it's the light. I only figured it out because {family} told me.
When it didn't work it told me "move away from the light, the card has a reflection". I moved and it worked. At least it told me why.
Fine. Standard ID scan.
The app froze on the camera screen. I had to close it and the whole thing started from the beginning.
The selfie part, eish. It said blink, then turn your head, then smile. I did it and it said "liveness check failed". I don't even know what that means. I tried five times, then I stopped.
The selfie was quick. I just looked at the camera and it did its thing.
I'm not used to taking pictures of myself. My hands shake. By the time I was in the circle it said time's up.
I did it but I'm not happy about a bank having my face. Where does that picture go after?
It says my face doesn't match my ID. The ID photo is from when I was 16! Of course I look different.
I liked that it showed a little picture of what to do first, like a cartoon person turning their head. So when it was my turn I already knew. My first time doing this, and it worked.
Face thing didn't work. Tried a lot.

My daughter kept walking into the camera because she wanted to see. Then the dog barked and I turned. It failed every time I moved even a little. You need a quiet room for this thing, and in my house there isn't one.
The face scan worked the second time. First time I had my cap on, my mistake.
The front camera on my phone is very bad. I had to borrow {family}'s phone, then the app said it's a new device and wanted the SMS again.
Face check done in seconds. Nice.
After the selfie it said "verifying" for very long. I didn't know if I must wait or if it was stuck. I waited ten minutes and closed it.
It said "please ensure adequate lighting and remove accessories". I took off my earrings, but I didn't know if my doek counts. Then I took that off too just to be safe.
When it failed it told me "try again with your face closer". The second time it was fine.
Last year someone opened accounts using my name. Now an app wants my face? I want to do this in a branch, with a person.

The OTP took more than five minutes to come. By the time it came the app said it expired. I pressed resend and the same thing. Where I stay the network is bad in the evening. Third time I went outside and stood by the gate and then it worked.
I asked for the code three times and then it said I'm blocked for 24 hours. I didn't even do anything wrong, the SMS just didn't come.
OTP came straight away. Good.
It read the SMS code by itself, I didn't even have to type it. That's nice.
The OTP came, a bit slow, but it came.
I got two SMSes with two different codes and I didn't know which one is the right one. I used the first one. Wrong.
My SIM is in the old phone and the app is on the other phone. So I was running between two phones to get the code.

The SMS said "never share this code with anyone". Then the app asked me for the code. I stopped there because I thought, is this a scam? Only later {family} explained it's okay to put it in the app, just not tell a person.
Normal OTP.
It wanted the code sent to my old number. I don't use that number anymore and there was no way to change it in the app. I had to go to the branch.
It told me "we sent a code to 082... check your SMS". So I knew exactly where to look. Some apps don't say.

Proof of address is my biggest problem. The house is in my mother's name, the electricity is prepaid, so there's no bill. I rent a room, there's no lease. Where must I get proof of address from? I stopped there.
I don't have a bill in my name. Everything is in my landlord's name. I sell at the taxi rank, nobody gives me letters.
I had to go ask the councillor's office for a letter. It took two days but they gave me one. The app took it. Long story for one paper.
I liked that I could just type my address and say "I live here" without uploading a bill. That made it easy, because I don't have bills.
It never said at the beginning that I'll need proof of address. If it did I would have got it ready. Now I'm stuck in the middle.

They want proof of address but the landlord won't give me anything in writing because he doesn't want problems with SARS. So I can't open the account, and I can't get paid into an account. It's a circle.
Uploaded my municipal account. Fine.

It said if you don't have a bill, you can use an affidavit from the police station, and it even showed what the affidavit must say. I went to the police station in the morning and finished in the afternoon.
It wanted a PDF. My bill is paper. I took a photo but it said wrong format. How do I make a PDF on my phone?
It said the bill must be less than three months old. Mine is from four months ago. Now I must wait for the next one.
I used my child's school letter with my address. I wasn't sure it will work but it did. Lucky.
Proof of address. That's where I stopped.

It asked "who is your employer" and "what's your monthly salary". I sell vetkoek. Some days I make R400, some days R50. There's no box for that. I chose "self-employed" and then it wanted a company registration number.
There was no option for SASSA. I had to choose "other" and then type it. It made me feel like my money is not real money.
The income questions were simple. Just pick a range, not the exact amount. I liked that.
It asked how much I earn and what I spend. I don't know what I spend exactly, I just guessed. I hope it doesn't matter.
Why does a bank want to know my income for a normal account? I'm not asking for a loan.
Payslip upload, done.
It wanted three months of bank statements to prove my income. But the reason I'm opening the account is because I don't have a bank account. Where must I get statements?
I'm a student and I do deliveries on the side. I didn't know which one to choose. Student or self-employed? I chose student.
"Source of funds" and "source of wealth"... are those not the same thing? I put salary in both.
It had "social grant" as an option. That was nice, I didn't have to explain.
Answered. Nothing to say.
It asked my employer twice, once in the details and once here. Like nobody is reading.

There were four accounts and each one had a list of things. I read them, I didn't see the difference. They all say "free" this and "R5" that. In the end I chose the one in the middle because I didn't want the cheapest, and I didn't want the expensive one.
It just asked me what I need it for, salary, saving or business, and then it showed me one account. Didn't have to compare.
I chose the free one. I hope it's really free. These things always have small costs later.
"Monthly management fee", "pay-as-you-transact"... I don't know these words. Just tell me how much it costs per month.
I liked that there was one for people who sell. It said I can see my sales and the money separate from my own money. That's exactly my problem at home, everything mixes.
I chose one, then I wanted to go back and look at the other one again, and it took me back to the start.
Picked the basic one.
The savings one had an interest rate but it didn't say what I'll actually get on, like, R500. Percent means nothing to me.
The comparison table was clear. I could see the fees side by side. Took me a minute to decide.
I wanted to ask somebody which one is better for me but there was no one to ask. At the branch you can ask the lady. Here I'm alone with my phone.
It kept pushing the credit card. I said no twice and it asked again on the next page.
The fees were at the bottom in small letters. I only saw them after. Cash withdrawal R10, notifications R1 each... for me R10 is a loaf of bread. These things must be at the top.
It showed me straight away, "this account costs R7.50 a month". One number. That's all I wanted to know.
I'm scared of fees. My last bank took money every month and I didn't know for what. Here also I don't really understand.
Fees look okay, same as other banks more or less.
Too many small fees. I can't follow.
It said I can draw my grant money for free at the shops. That's important to me because my grant is small and I don't want R10 taken every time.
The fee page is fine, but it would help if it said what I'd pay in a normal month based on what I do. Like an estimate.
"Excluding VAT"... so how much is it with VAT? Just give me the real number.
I didn't read it. Nobody reads that.
It's like twenty pages. On a phone. I just scrolled down and ticked.

There was a box that said I agree they can share my information with "partners". Which partners? I don't want people calling me selling insurance. I ticked because it won't let me go further without ticking.
I liked the short version with five points. I actually read those. The long one I didn't.
I ticked everything. I don't know what I agreed to, honestly.
The marketing tick was already ticked. That's sneaky. I unticked it.
Short and clear. Good.
I asked my son to read it for me. He said it's normal. So I agreed.
When it said "your account is open" with my account number right there, I was happy. I screenshot it and sent it to my boss the same day so I can get paid. That's what I needed.
It showed my account number and a button to share it. Easy.
It said "we're reviewing your application, we'll let you know". It's been two days. I don't know if it's yes or no.
The account is open but the card I must go fetch at a branch. The nearest one is in town, R30 taxi there and back. So what's the point of opening on the app?
It gave me a card on the phone straight away. I could use it before the real card even comes. That's clever.
It said "pending". Pending what? For how long? Must I do something?
Done. Account open.
It finished, but I never got an SMS or email that it's done. I didn't trust it until I checked the next day.
At the end it told me exactly what happens next: card comes in 5 days, I'll get an SMS, I can collect at Boxer. I like when I know what happens next. I didn't have to phone anyone.
After it said done, I couldn't find my account number again. I had to look all over the app.
Opened in like ten minutes. Not bad.

To add my landlord I needed the account number, the bank, the branch code and a "reference". He only gave me the account number on WhatsApp. I had to message him again and wait. By then I had forgotten what I was doing in the app.
I just picked the bank and it filled the branch code by itself. I remember when you had to know the branch code. This is better.
It added the person but I wasn't sure if the name is right. It doesn't show me the name of the account owner. What if I typed one number wrong and the money goes to a stranger?

When I put the account number it showed "account holder: T Mokoena". That's my sister, so I knew it's correct. That made me relax, because I made a mistake once at another bank and never got that money back.
Adding someone took a bit but it's a once-off thing, so it's fine.
"Recipient reference" and "my reference"... which one does the other person see? I always mix them up.
It wanted an OTP just to add a person. Then another one to pay. Too much.
I added my mother with just her cellphone number. Didn't need her account details. Nice.
Most people I pay are not in a bank. So beneficiaries don't really help me.
I couldn't find where to add a new person. It's hiding under "Transact", then "Pay", then a plus at the top. Why not just "Add person"?

I paid my rent in like a minute. Choose the person, put the amount, it shows the summary, I confirm, done. And then it showed the proof of payment straight away so I sent it to the landlord on WhatsApp.
The money left my account but the other person didn't get it until the next day. It never said it will take long. My landlord thought I was lying.
It only told me there's a fee for immediate payment after I already pressed pay. R10 for my R{amount}? If I knew, I would have chosen the normal one. Show me the fee before, not after.
Paying is fine. I've done it many times on other apps, it's the same.
The confirm button is right next to cancel and both are small. I pressed cancel by mistake twice.
Fast. Easy. No complaints.
It said I'm over my limit. What limit? I never set a limit. And it didn't tell me how to change it.
Every time I pay it takes money for the payment. When you only have R{amount} you feel every rand. I've started taking out cash and paying people cash, it's cheaper.
I liked that it said "your money will arrive in 1-2 days" before I paid. So I knew to pay earlier.
In the middle of paying the app said "session expired". Did it go or not? I had to call the bank to check.
It works but it's a lot of taps for something I do every week. Let me save my rent payment and just press it.
There's "pay again" next to last month's payment. I just pressed it. Took ten seconds.
"Transaction could not be completed." Why?
Buying data is easy, three taps. I do it every few days so that matters.

I bought electricity and the money went off but the token didn't come. I waited an hour. Meanwhile we're sitting in the dark. Then I got the token by SMS late at night. It never told me there's a delay.
It remembers my meter number. Before I always had to go find the little card on the meter box outside. Now it's just "buy again". That's the thing I use the most.
Airtime and data is fine. Same as everywhere.
There are too many bundles to choose from. Daily, weekly, monthly, night, social... I just want normal data.
The token came with 20 numbers. I didn't know if I must type all of them in the meter. Spaces or no spaces?
Electricity in a minute. Good.
Where's electricity? I looked under "Pay" and it wasn't there. It's under "Buy". To me paying for electricity is paying.

I send money to my mother in Limpopo every month. She doesn't have a bank account. Here I put her number, the amount, and she gets an SMS with a PIN and she draws at Shoprite. It's cheaper than taking a taxi to go give her the money.
The fee for sending R200 was R10. That's 5 percent. It said it nowhere until the end.

My brother went to the till to draw the money and the cashier said the PIN is wrong. I checked, the PIN was right. He stood there with people behind him. It worked the second day. I don't know what happened and the app said nothing.
Cash send works. Nothing special.
I can send money to my wife and she can draw it at the shop. Before I used a guy who charges a lot. This is cheaper.
There's a limit of R3,000. I wanted to send for school fees and I had to do it in two goes and pay two fees.
Sent in a minute. She got it.
The proof of payment opens as a picture and I can share it on WhatsApp. That's what everybody asks for, the POP.
After I paid, it just went back to the home screen. No "done", nothing. I checked my balance to see if it really went.
The proof of payment is a PDF that only opens with some special app. My landlord on his old phone can't open it. I had to screenshot the screen instead and he said it's not proper proof.
Got the confirmation. Fine.
It showed in big letters "Payment successful" with a tick and the amount. That's all I need to see.
After I paid I got an SMS, an email and a notification all saying the same thing. One is enough.

Making our stokvel group on the app was easy. I put the name, how much each person pays, the day, and then it gave me a link to share on our WhatsApp group. By the evening nine of our twelve members had joined.

To open the group account it wanted the constitution, minutes from a meeting, and IDs of three signatories. We are twelve ladies who've been doing this for eleven years with a notebook. We don't have minutes. It made us feel like we're not proper.
The chairlady sent a link and said join. I didn't click straight away because these days links on WhatsApp are scams. I first phoned her to check.
Setting up took some time, but it's a once-off. We'll see how it works month to month.
Two of our members don't have smartphones. They can't join the app. So now we're half on the app and half paying cash to me, which is worse than before.
I liked that I could choose the rules: how much, which date, and the order of who gets paid out. It's like our notebook but on the phone.
It asked "is the group a legal entity". I don't know. We're a stokvel. Is that a yes?
Joined. My sister did it for me.
I'm with {other_bank}. It wanted me to open an account at this bank to join. I don't want two banks just for the stokvel.
What I liked is that the money goes into a group account and not into somebody's personal account. Last time our treasurer "borrowed" from the stokvel money.
When I pay my R{amount}, everyone in the group can see I paid. No more arguing at the meeting about who paid and who didn't. That used to cause fights in our stokvel, really.
Paying in from my other bank costs me a fee every month. So now my contribution is more than everyone else's.

My grant comes on the 3rd but the stokvel debit order goes off on the 1st. Two months now it bounced and I got charged for that too. I asked the treasurer to change the date and she says the app only allows one date for everybody.
It sends a reminder two days before I must pay. I forget easily, so that helps me.
I pay on the app, it's fine. Some months I still give cash at the meeting when I don't have it on the phone.
Some members pay by EFT with their own reference, like "Mama T" or "stokvel". The app doesn't know who it is. I still have to check every payment one by one.
It matches who paid automatically and shows me a list with ticks. The ones who didn't pay are in red. I used to spend a whole Sunday with my notebook.
I sell at the market, so I have cash, not money in the bank. I have to go deposit it first and pay a fee for that, then pay the stokvel.
Paying works. Nothing to say.
I could see when it's my turn for the payout, it's in August. I'm planning school uniform for my kids around that. It's nice to see it on the phone and not just remember what the chairlady said.
For the payout two of us have to approve on the app. The other signatory was in Durban with no data for a week. So the payout was late and the member was very angry with me, not with the app.
My payout said "processing" for three days. In December. Everybody needs their money in December.
The December payout came on the day it said. Straight to my account. No standing in the bank queue with cash in my bag, which is dangerous.
We still do the groceries the normal way. We just use the app to collect.
When the payout came, there was less than I expected. There was a fee for the payout. Nobody told us.
I can download a statement for the meeting with every member's payments. I printed it and everybody could see. People trust it more than my handwriting, haha.
I can't find the history of last year. It only shows six months. Our year runs from January to December.
One member paid cash at the meeting. There's no way to add that on the app. So the app says she didn't pay and she's upset with me. Cash still happens, the app must allow that.
I just check that my payment shows. I don't look at the rest.
I can see the balance but not what money went out and why. The treasurer can see more than us. That's not fair, it's all our money.
Everyone can see the balance. It stopped a lot of the "where's the money" talk in our group.
Everything is hidden behind the three lines at the top. I spent five minutes looking for "statement". In the end I found it under "Documents", which I would never think of.
The main things are at the bottom, big buttons: pay, buy, cards. I don't have to search.
I pressed something and ended up somewhere I didn't want. Then I couldn't find the way back to the start. I closed the app and opened it again.
I'll get used to it. The first time is always confusing with a new app.
There's no back button on some pages. My phone's back button closes the whole app.
Easy to find things.
Too many menus inside menus. I just want search. Let me type "statement" and go there.
I only use three things in the app. The rest I don't touch. So it's fine for me.
The words are bank words. "Debit order mandate", "available versus current balance"... I have money or I don't have money. Why are there two balances? Nobody ever explained that to me.
It talks normal. "Send money", "your money", not those big bank words. I liked that.
I wanted it in Sesotho. I can read English but in my language I understand faster, especially the money things.
English is fine for me. Some words are long but I get it.
What is "authenticate"? Just say "check it's you".
I could switch it to isiZulu. Not everything was in isiZulu, but the main parts were. My mother can also use it now.
Too many bank words.
The isiXhosa translation is a bit strange. It's like someone used Google. My English is better than that isiXhosa, so I put it back to English. But for older people it's still good that it's there.
Every time I open the app it loads pictures and adverts. I'm paying for that data. Just show me my balance. I check my balance more than anything, and each time it's eating my data.
I saw it doesn't use my data, it says "zero-rated". That's why I use the app now instead of going to the ATM.
It takes long to open. The circle just keeps going around. In the queue at the till I don't have that time.
Fast. Opens quickly.
Speed is okay. Sometimes slow in the evening, but my network is also slow then.
In my area the app just says "no connection" even when WhatsApp is working. WhatsApp works, the bank doesn't. How?
My phone is old and the app is heavy. It hangs every time. I've stopped using it, I use the USSD code instead.

It said "Error 4021. Please try again later." What is 4021? Later when? I tried later. Same thing. There's no number to call on that screen, nothing. I just gave up and went to the branch on Saturday.
When something went wrong it told me in normal words what happened and what to do. "Your ID photo is blurry, try again in better light." That I can fix.
An error came and everything I filled in was wiped. Start again from zero.
One error, I tried again, it worked. Normal.
"Something went wrong." Thanks.
The error message made me feel like I did something wrong. "Invalid input." I typed what it asked.
It failed at the end but when I came back, everything was still there. I just pressed submit again.
I like that it asks for my fingerprint before paying. My children play games on my phone. Now I know they can't send money by mistake.

I don't trust doing banking on the phone. My neighbour lost R8,000 because someone phoned her pretending to be the bank. Now when the app asks for a code, I get scared. Even if this one is real, how do I know?
Too much security. PIN, then OTP, then fingerprint, for R50 airtime. I understand safety but it's too much for small things.
It showed a message "the bank will never phone you to ask for your PIN". That's good, older people need to be reminded.
It feels safe, I think. I don't really know how to tell.
It wanted access to my contacts, my location and my photos. Why does a bank want my photos?
Feels safe. Good.
I'm half-half. The app looks proper, but you hear so many stories. I keep only a little money in the account and the rest I keep in the stokvel. Maybe after some months I'll trust it more.

The chat is a robot. I asked my question three different ways and it kept sending me the same link. I wanted a person. When I finally got the number, it was 40 minutes waiting with that music. My airtime finished.
I sent a WhatsApp and a real person answered in a few minutes. Sorted out my problem. That I didn't expect from a bank.
There's no "call me" option. I don't have airtime to phone them.
I didn't need help, so I don't know.
There was a little video showing how to do it. I watched it twice and then did it myself.
I looked for help and couldn't find it. Help must be on every page, not hidden.
It looks clean, not too busy. Colours are nice. It looks like a proper bank.
The grey writing on the white is hard to read in the sun. I stood in the shade to read.
The home screen has adverts for loans and insurance everywhere. I just want to see my money.
Looks fine.
Looks modern. Better than the old app. Dark mode is nice.
I made the letters big on my phone but the app doesn't follow. Everything else on my phone is big, then I open the bank app and it's tiny again. My eyes are not what they were.
The buttons are big. Even with my big thumbs I don't press the wrong one.
There's too much on one screen. Numbers, graphs, tips... my head gets tired.

My ID number, then my ID number again to "confirm". If I typed it wrong the first time I'll type it wrong again.

My phone doesn't have a good camera. The picture always comes out with lines. I asked my neighbour to use hers, then the app said this phone is not registered to me. Round and round.

I was worried about the selfie because my friend said it failed for her many times. For me it worked straight away. It said "look straight", then "turn left", and it was finished. I don't know what she was doing.

Face scan, one go. Clean.

I had to wait for the baby to sleep before I could do it, because she wants to be in every picture. Once she was asleep it was fine. But it's not something you can do on the go.

After the selfie the screen said "hold on, we're checking" and then nothing. No yes, no no. I waited, I pressed back, it started the selfie again. I did the selfie three times in total and I still don't know if it worked or not.

I went to the police station for the affidavit like it said. The queue was long, I had my baby on my back, then the officer said come back tomorrow, the commissioner is not here. That's one day of my life just for this.

There was an option "I earn money from selling or doing jobs". Finally somebody thought of us. It asked roughly how much in a good week and a bad week. That's how my money works.

Our chairlady sent the link on WhatsApp. I clicked, put my ID number, and it showed "Masakhane Ladies, 14 members". My name was already there because she added it. I just said yes. Easier than I thought.
I liked that it showed who the treasurer and chairlady are, with their pictures. So I knew it's our group and not some scam.
I added all our members from my contacts. It took maybe fifteen minutes. The rest they did themselves.
Joining was fine. The real test is if the money comes when it's my turn.

We had to choose between a "registered" group and a "simple" group. Simple was quick, but then the limit is lower. We save R60,000 a year together, so we needed the other one, and that one wanted the papers. We're still busy with the papers.
Some of the older ladies don't want to be on the app. They say they want to see the money. We'll see if they come around.
Every member must be approved by me one by one. With twenty members that's twenty times the same thing.
It asked if I'm a "beneficiary" or a "signatory". I'm a member. Those words are not stokvel words.

The bank wants three signatories. In our group nobody wants to be a signatory, because they think if money goes missing they'll be blamed. It took us two meetings to get three people. The app made it sound like a quick click.
I don't like that the bank sees our stokvel money.
I can choose to pay on the 4th, after my grant comes. That's important for me. I'm never late now.
Paying the stokvel is like paying anybody. Pick the group, the amount is already there, pay. Two taps.

Every time someone pays, I get a message: "Thandi paid R500 for June". By the 5th I can see who's still outstanding and I send them a reminder from the app. Before, I was calling people and it caused bad feelings. Now the app is the bad guy, not me.
I still pay cash to the treasurer, and she puts it on the app. It's fine as long as she does it.
I pay, it shows. Okay.
I pay R300, but R6 goes to fees. So in a year I paid R72 just to pay my stokvel. Nobody told us that.

My money is cash from selling. To pay the stokvel on the app, I must first go deposit at the ATM, which charges me, then pay from the app, which charges me again. With the old way I just give my cash at the meeting. The app made it more expensive for me.
When two people pay the same amount on the same day with no name, I can't tell who's who. I still have to phone them.
Every month it wants an OTP to pay the stokvel. It's the same payment.

My turn was in January, perfect for school things. The money was in my account the morning of the 15th like it said. I didn't have to go fetch cash from anybody's house. I took the kids to buy uniform the same day.
Doing the payout is easy now. I press approve, the second signatory gets a message, she approves, done. No more carrying cash.
The payout came. A day late, but it came.
It said my payout is "scheduled". I didn't know what that means. Then it came the next day.
One signatory changed her phone and couldn't log in for two weeks. The whole group's payout was stuck because of one person's phone.

For the grocery stokvel we buy in bulk at Makro in December. The app has a daily limit, so the treasurer couldn't pay the whole amount at once. She had to split it over three days. On the last day the special was finished.
Less money came than I expected.
At the end of the year I pressed "group statement" and it made a nice PDF with everyone's payments. I read it out at the meeting. Nobody argued.
I can see everything. That's good.
I only look at my own payments. The rest is the treasurer's job.
Our rule is if you're late, you pay R50 fine. The app doesn't know about our fines. So I keep the fines in my notebook and the payments on the app. Two places. Better than before, but not finished.
To see who paid in March I must go month by month. I want one page with everyone and all the months, like my notebook.
When the treasurer took out money for the funeral, it didn't say what it was for. Just "withdrawal R5,000". Now people are talking.
